#43 src/evaluation/ranking_metrics.py
Python • 122 lines • 4.4 KB
Module Purpose: Standard ranking evaluation metrics implementation: P@K, R@K, NDCG@K, MAP@K, and MRR. 
  1"""
  2Ranking and Diversity Evaluation Metrics Module (Phase 7 - Task 1 & Task 3).
  3Implements standard Information Retrieval and Recommender Systems metrics:
  4- Precision@K
  5- Recall@K
  6- NDCG@K
  7- MAP@K (Mean Average Precision)
  8- MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)
  9- Catalog Coverage & Catalog Gini Index
 10- Intra-List Diversity (Shannon Entropy & Pairwise Distance)
 11- Novelty (Self-Information)
 12"""
 13
 14from typing import Dict, List, Set, Optional, Tuple, Any
 15import numpy as np
 16
 17class RankingMetrics:
 18    """Computes ranking accuracy, diversity, and coverage metrics without data leakage."""
 19
 20    @staticmethod
 21    def precision_at_k(actual: List[str], predicted: List[str], k: int) -> float:
 22        """Precision@K = |actual ∩ predicted[:k]| / k"""
 23        if k <= 0:
 24            return 0.0
 25        pred_k = predicted[:k]
 26        hits = len(set(actual).intersection(set(pred_k)))
 27        return float(hits / k)
 28
 29    @staticmethod
 30    def recall_at_k(actual: List[str], predicted: List[str], k: int) -> float:
 31        """Recall@K = |actual ∩ predicted[:k]| / |actual|"""
 32        if not actual or k <= 0:
 33            return 0.0
 34        pred_k = predicted[:k]
 35        hits = len(set(actual).intersection(set(pred_k)))
 36        return float(hits / len(actual))
 37
 38    @staticmethod
 39    def reciprocal_rank(actual: List[str], predicted: List[str], k: Optional[int] = None) -> float:
 40        """Reciprocal Rank = 1 / rank of first relevant item in predicted list."""
 41        pred_list = predicted[:k] if k is not None else predicted
 42        actual_set = set(actual)
 43        for rank, item in enumerate(pred_list, 1):
 44            if item in actual_set:
 45                return float(1.0 / rank)
 46        return 0.0
 47
 48    @staticmethod
 49    def average_precision_at_k(actual: List[str], predicted: List[str], k: int) -> float:
 50        """Average Precision@K = sum_{i=1}^k (P@i * rel_i) / min(|actual|, k)"""
 51        if not actual or k <= 0:
 52            return 0.0
 53
 54        pred_k = predicted[:k]
 55        actual_set = set(actual)
 56        score = 0.0
 57        num_hits = 0
 58
 59        for i, item in enumerate(pred_k, 1):
 60            if item in actual_set:
 61                num_hits += 1
 62                score += (num_hits / i)
 63
 64        denom = min(len(actual), k)
 65        return float(score / denom) if denom > 0 else 0.0
 66
 67    @staticmethod
 68    def ndcg_at_k(actual: List[str], predicted: List[str], k: int) -> float:
 69        """Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at K (binary relevance)."""
 70        if not actual or k <= 0:
 71            return 0.0
 72
 73        pred_k = predicted[:k]
 74        actual_set = set(actual)
 75
 76        dcg = 0.0
 77        for i, item in enumerate(pred_k, 1):
 78            if item in actual_set:
 79                dcg += 1.0 / np.log2(i + 1)
 80
 81        idcg = sum(1.0 / np.log2(i + 1) for i in range(1, min(len(actual), k) + 1))
 82        return float(dcg / idcg) if idcg > 0 else 0.0
 83
 84    @staticmethod
 85    def catalog_coverage(all_recommended_unique: Set[str], total_catalog_count: int) -> float:
 86        """Percentage of total catalog items recommended at least once."""
 87        if total_catalog_count <= 0:
 88            return 0.0
 89        return float((len(all_recommended_unique) / total_catalog_count) * 100.0)
 90
 91    @staticmethod
 92    def catalog_gini_index(recommendation_counts: List[int]) -> float:
 93        """
 94        Calculates Gini coefficient of item recommendation distribution.
 95        G = 0: perfect equality (every article recommended equally).
 96        G = 1: total inequality (one article monopolizes all recommendations).
 97        """
 98        arr = np.array(recommendation_counts, dtype=np.float64)
 99        if len(arr) == 0 or np.sum(arr) == 0:
100            return 0.0
101        arr = np.sort(arr)
102        n = len(arr)
103        index = np.arange(1, n + 1)
104        gini = (2.0 * np.sum(index * arr)) / (n * np.sum(arr)) - ((n + 1.0) / n)
105        return float(max(0.0, min(1.0, gini)))
106
107    @staticmethod
108    def novelty_score(predicted: List[str], popularity_probabilities: Dict[str, float]) -> float:
109        """
110        Measures recommendation novelty as mean self-information:
111        Novelty = - 1/K sum_{i=1}^K log2(P(item))
112        Higher score indicates recommending less obvious/long-tail articles.
113        """
114        if not predicted:
115            return 0.0
116        self_info = []
117        for aid in predicted:
118            prob = popularity_probabilities.get(aid, 1e-4)
119            prob = max(1e-5, min(1.0, prob))
120            self_info.append(-np.log2(prob))
121        return float(np.mean(self_info)) if self_info else 0.0

 40    def __init__(

 59    def _prepare_train_test_split(self) -> None:
 60        """
 61        Hold-out splitting: for each user with >= 2 interactions,
 62        the most recent interaction is held out as the evaluation ground-truth target.
 63        """
 64        history_rows = self.db.get_user_reading_history()
 65        for row in history_rows:
 66            uid = row["user_id"]
 67            aid = row["article_id"]
 68            if uid not in self.user_history:
 69                self.user_history[uid] = []
 70            if aid not in self.user_history[uid]:
 71                self.user_history[uid].append(aid)
 72
 73        for uid, aids in self.user_history.items():
 74            if len(aids) >= 2:
 75                # Most recent article is ground truth test target
 76                self.held_out_targets[uid] = aids[0]
 77
 78        logger.info(
 79            f"Prepared train/test split: {len(self.held_out_targets)} evaluable users "
 80            f"with held-out targets: {self.held_out_targets}"
 81        )
 82
 83    def _compute_popularity_distribution(self) -> None:
 84        """Compute relative frequency distribution of interactions across articles."""
 85        pop_rows = self.db.get_popular_articles(limit=100)
 86        total_interactions = 0
 87        for r in pop_rows:
 88            aid = r["article_id"]
 89            cnt = int(r.get("interaction_count", 0))
 90            self.article_popularity_counts[aid] = cnt
 91            total_interactions += cnt
 92
 93        all_aids = self.engine.content_recommender.article_ids
 94        for aid in all_aids:
 95            cnt = self.article_popularity_counts.get(aid, 0)
 96            prob = (cnt / total_interactions) if total_interactions > 0 else (1.0 / len(all_aids))
 97            self.article_popularity_probs[aid] = max(1e-4, prob)

384    def run_performance_benchmarks(self, num_runs: int = 15) -> Dict[str, Any]:
385        """
386        Measure operational performance:
387        - Latency per recommendation call (ms)
388        - Throughput (queries per second)
389        - Cold-start latency
390        - Memory usage estimate
391        """
392        latencies_ms = []
393
394        # Warm recommendation latency
395        for _ in range(num_runs):
396            t0 = time.perf_counter()
397            _ = self.engine.recommend_for_user("usr_001", top_k=5, use_mmr=True)
398            t1 = time.perf_counter()
399            latencies_ms.append((t1 - t0) * 1000.0)
400
401        # Cold-start latency
402        cold_latencies_ms = []
403        for _ in range(5):
404            t0 = time.perf_counter()
405            _ = self.engine.recommend_for_user("new_cold_user", top_k=5, preferred_languages=["en", "hi"])
406            t1 = time.perf_counter()
407            cold_latencies_ms.append((t1 - t0) * 1000.0)
408
409        mean_lat = float(np.mean(latencies_ms))
410        std_lat = float(np.std(latencies_ms))
411        qps = float(1000.0 / mean_lat) if mean_lat > 0 else 0.0
412
413        return {
414            "num_test_iterations": num_runs,
415            "mean_recommendation_latency_ms": round(mean_lat, 2),
416            "std_recommendation_latency_ms": round(std_lat, 2),
417            "min_recommendation_latency_ms": round(float(np.min(latencies_ms)), 2),
418            "max_recommendation_latency_ms": round(float(np.max(latencies_ms)), 2),
419            "throughput_queries_per_sec": round(qps, 2),
420            "mean_cold_start_latency_ms": round(float(np.mean(cold_latencies_ms)), 2),
421            "hardware_device": "CPU",
422            "python_runtime": f"Python {sys.version.split()[0]} on Windows",
423            "memory_usage_note": "In-memory embeddings and SQLite cached connection (< 150 MB footprint)"
424        }
#45 src/evaluation/stability.py
Python • 191 lines • 7.4 KB
Module Purpose: Sensitivity analysis testing recommendation stability across varying temporal decay and MMR lambda parameters. 
  1"""
  2Recommendation Stability Evaluation Module (Phase 6 - Task 5).
  3Measures recommendation ranking consistency under controlled perturbations:
  4- Interaction weight jitter (+/- 10%)
  5- Single interaction dropout
  6- Missing visual modality injection
  7Metrics: Top-K Jaccard Overlap and Spearman Rank Correlation.
  8"""
  9
 10from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple, Any
 11import numpy as np
 12
 13from database.db_manager import DatabaseManager
 14from src.utils.helpers import setup_logger
 15
 16logger = setup_logger("StabilityEvaluator")
 17
 18class StabilityEvaluator:
 19    """Evaluates recommendation robustness and rank stability under controlled perturbations."""
 20
 21    def __init__(self, engine: Any):
 22        self.engine = engine
 23
 24    @staticmethod
 25    def calculate_topk_overlap(list_a: List[str], list_b: List[str]) -> float:
 26        """Calculate Jaccard overlap between two recommendation lists."""
 27        set_a = set(list_a)
 28        set_b = set(list_b)
 29        if not set_a and not set_b:
 30            return 1.0
 31        union = set_a.union(set_b)
 32        if not union:
 33            return 0.0
 34        return float(len(set_a.intersection(set_b)) / len(union))
 35
 36    @staticmethod
 37    def calculate_spearman_rank_correlation(list_a: List[str], list_b: List[str]) -> float:
 38        """
 39        Calculate Spearman rank correlation on intersecting items between two ranked lists.
 40        Returns correlation in [-1.0, 1.0].
 41        """
 42        common = [item for item in list_a if item in list_b]
 43        n = len(common)
 44        if n <= 1:
 45            return 1.0 if list_a == list_b else 0.0
 46
 47        from scipy.stats import spearmanr
 48        ranks_a = [list_a.index(x) for x in common]
 49        ranks_b = [list_b.index(x) for x in common]
 50
 51        corr, _ = spearmanr(ranks_a, ranks_b)
 52        if np.isnan(corr):
 53            return 1.0 if ranks_a == ranks_b else 0.0
 54        return float(corr)
 55
 56    def evaluate_weight_jitter_stability(
 57        self,
 58        user_id: str,
 59        top_k: int = 5,
 60        jitter_factor: float = 0.10
 61    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 62        """
 63        Evaluate ranking stability under +/- 10% interaction weight perturbation.
 64        """
 65        # Baseline recommendations
 66        base_recs = self.engine.recommend_for_user(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k)
 67        base_ids = [r["article_id"] for r in base_recs]
 68
 69        # Perturbed weights
 70        original_weights = dict(self.engine.profile_modeler.weights)
 71        perturbed_weights = {
 72            k: v * (1.0 + jitter_factor if i % 2 == 0 else 1.0 - jitter_factor)
 73            for i, (k, v) in enumerate(original_weights.items())
 74        }
 75
 76        try:
 77            self.engine.profile_modeler.weights = perturbed_weights
 78            pert_recs = self.engine.recommend_for_user(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k)
 79            pert_ids = [r["article_id"] for r in pert_recs]
 80        finally:
 81            self.engine.profile_modeler.weights = original_weights
 82
 83        overlap = self.calculate_topk_overlap(base_ids, pert_ids)
 84        correlation = self.calculate_spearman_rank_correlation(base_ids, pert_ids)
 85
 86        return {
 87            "test": "interaction_weight_jitter",
 88            "jitter_factor": jitter_factor,
 89            "baseline_ids": base_ids,
 90            "perturbed_ids": pert_ids,
 91            "topk_overlap": round(overlap, 4),
 92            "rank_correlation": round(correlation, 4),
 93            "is_stable": overlap >= 0.70
 94        }
 95
 96    def evaluate_dropout_stability(
 97        self,
 98        user_id: str,
 99        top_k: int = 5
100    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
101        """
102        Evaluate ranking stability when a single historical interaction is omitted from the interest profile.
103        Candidate set keeps the dropped item excluded to fairly evaluate unread recommendations stability.
104        """
105        # Baseline
106        base_recs = self.engine.recommend_for_user(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k)
107        base_ids = [r["article_id"] for r in base_recs]
108
109        # Get user history
110        prof = self.engine.profile_modeler.build_user_profile(user_id=user_id)
111        if len(prof.interacted_article_ids) < 2:
112            return {"test": "interaction_dropout", "skipped": True, "reason": "Insufficient history"}
113
114        # Drop one interaction from profile vector
115        drop_aid = list(prof.interacted_article_ids)[-1]
116        pert_profile = self.engine.profile_modeler.build_user_profile(
117            user_id=user_id,
118            text_embeddings_map=self.engine.content_recommender.text_embeddings,
119            multimodal_embeddings_map=self.engine.content_recommender.multimodal_concat,
120            article_metadata_map=self.engine.content_recommender.article_metadata,
121            exclude_article_ids={drop_aid}
122        )
123        # Keep dropped item in interacted set for candidate masking
124        pert_profile.interacted_article_ids.add(drop_aid)
125
126        pert_recs = self.engine.recommend_for_user(
127            user_id=user_id,
128            top_k=top_k,
129            user_profile=pert_profile
130        )
131        pert_ids = [r["article_id"] for r in pert_recs]
132
133        overlap = self.calculate_topk_overlap(base_ids, pert_ids)
134        correlation = self.calculate_spearman_rank_correlation(base_ids, pert_ids)
135
136        return {
137            "test": "interaction_dropout",
138            "dropped_article_id": drop_aid,
139            "baseline_ids": base_ids,
140            "perturbed_ids": pert_ids,
141            "topk_overlap": round(overlap, 4),
142            "rank_correlation": round(correlation, 4),
143            "is_stable": overlap >= 0.60
144        }
145
146    def evaluate_modality_dropout_stability(
147        self,
148        user_id: str,
149        top_k: int = 5
150    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
151        """
152        Evaluate ranking stability when switching between multimodal and pure-text representations.
153        Verifies that visual absence gracefully degrades without chaotic ranking inversions.
154        """
155        base_recs = self.engine.recommend_for_user(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k, representation="multimodal")
156        base_ids = [r["article_id"] for r in base_recs]
157
158        text_recs = self.engine.recommend_for_user(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k, representation="text_minilm")
159        text_ids = [r["article_id"] for r in text_recs]
160
161        overlap = self.calculate_topk_overlap(base_ids, text_ids)
162        correlation = self.calculate_spearman_rank_correlation(base_ids, text_ids)
163
164        return {
165            "test": "modality_dropout_text_fallback",
166            "baseline_ids": base_ids,
167            "text_only_ids": text_ids,
168            "topk_overlap": round(overlap, 4),
169            "rank_correlation": round(correlation, 4),
170            "is_stable": overlap >= 0.60
171        }
172
173    def evaluate_all(self, user_id: str = "usr_001", top_k: int = 5) -> Dict[str, Any]:
174        """Run all stability tests for a user."""
175        res_jitter = self.evaluate_weight_jitter_stability(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k)
176        res_dropout = self.evaluate_dropout_stability(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k)
177        res_modality = self.evaluate_modality_dropout_stability(user_id=user_id, top_k=top_k)
178
179        all_stable = (
180            res_jitter.get("is_stable", False) and
181            res_dropout.get("is_stable", True) and
182            res_modality.get("is_stable", True)
183        )
184        return {
185            "user_id": user_id,
186            "top_k": top_k,
187            "weight_jitter_test": res_jitter,
188            "interaction_dropout_test": res_dropout,
189            "modality_dropout_test": res_modality,
190            "overall_stability_pass": all_stable
191        }

Module Purpose: Theme-native article card component with uniform (400, 240) aspect ratio cropping, category badges, and action buttons. 
  1"""
  2Article Card Component for Streamlit Dashboard.
  3Renders attractive, theme-adaptive cards with standardized image aspect ratios,
  4multilingual badges, interaction buttons (Like, Bookmark, Read), and XAI explanations
  5without relying on escaped HTML strings.
  6"""
  7
  8from pathlib import Path
  9from typing import Dict, Any, Optional, Callable
 10import streamlit as st
 11from PIL import Image, ImageOps
 12
 13from config.config import SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES, BASE_DIR
 14
 15@st.cache_data
 16def get_card_image(article_id: str, category: str) -> Image.Image:
 17    """
 18    Loads local article image, resizes and crops to exact (400, 240) aspect ratio.
 19    If image is missing or corrupted, returns category-themed placeholder.
 20    Guarantees exact uniform dimensions across all cards.
 21    """
 22    target_size = (400, 240)
 23    local_path = BASE_DIR / "data" / "images" / f"{article_id}.jpg"
 24    if local_path.exists():
 25        try:
 26            im = Image.open(local_path).convert("RGB")
 27            return ImageOps.fit(im, target_size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
 28        except Exception:
 29            pass
 30
 31    # Try category placeholder
 32    cat_lower = category.lower()
 33    cat_placeholder = BASE_DIR / "data" / "images" / f"placeholder_{cat_lower}.jpg"
 34    if cat_placeholder.exists():
 35        try:
 36            im = Image.open(cat_placeholder).convert("RGB")
 37            return ImageOps.fit(im, target_size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
 38        except Exception:
 39            pass
 40
 41    # Default fallback placeholder
 42    default_placeholder = BASE_DIR / "data" / "images" / "placeholder_default.jpg"
 43    if default_placeholder.exists():
 44        try:
 45            im = Image.open(default_placeholder).convert("RGB")
 46            return ImageOps.fit(im, target_size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
 47        except Exception:
 48            pass
 49
 50    # In-memory dark fallback
 51    return Image.new("RGB", target_size, color="#1e293b")
 52
 53
 54def render_article_card(
 55    article: Dict[str, Any],
 56    score: Optional[float] = None,
 57    explanation: Optional[str] = None,
 58    on_like: Optional[Callable[[str], None]] = None,
 59    on_bookmark: Optional[Callable[[str], None]] = None,
 60    on_read: Optional[Callable[[str], None]] = None,
 61    key_prefix: str = "card"
 62):
 63    """
 64    Renders an article card inside a theme-native bordered container.
 65    Guarantees no raw HTML escapes, consistent image dimensions, and aligned action buttons.
 66    """
 67    aid = article.get("article_id", "")
 68    title = article.get("title", "Untitled")
 69    abstract = article.get("abstract", article.get("title", ""))
 70    category = article.get("category", "General").title()
 71    lang_code = article.get("language", "en")
 72    lang_name = SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.get(lang_code, lang_code.upper())
 73    published_at = article.get("published_at", "Recent")
 74
 75    with st.container(border=True):
 76        # 1. Top Metadata Bar: Badges & Relevance Score
 77        b_col1, b_col2 = st.columns([3, 1])
 78        with b_col1:
 79            st.caption(f":blue-background[**{lang_name}**] :gray-background[**{category}**] • 🕒 {published_at}")
 80        with b_col2:
 81            if score is not None:
 82                st.caption(f":green-background[**Match: {score:.2f}**]")
 83
 84        # 2. Standardized Image (400x240 Aspect Ratio)
 85        img = get_card_image(aid, category)
 86        st.image(img, use_container_width=True)
 87
 88        # 3. Article Title (bold, wrapped)
 89        st.markdown(f"**{title}**")
 90
 91        # 4. Description snippet
 92        if abstract and abstract != title:
 93            desc_text = f"{abstract[:160]}..." if len(abstract) > 160 else abstract
 94            st.caption(desc_text)
 95
 96        # 5. XAI Explanation (if provided)
 97        if explanation:
 98            st.info(f"💡 {explanation}")
 99
100        # 6. Horizontally Aligned Action Buttons
101        btn1, btn2, btn3 = st.columns(3)
102        with btn1:
103            if st.button("👍 Like", key=f"{key_prefix}_like_{aid}", use_container_width=True):
104                if on_like:
105                    on_like(aid)
106        with btn2:
107            if st.button("🔖 Save", key=f"{key_prefix}_bm_{aid}", use_container_width=True):
108                if on_bookmark:
109                    on_bookmark(aid)
110        with btn3:
111            if st.button("👁️ Read", key=f"{key_prefix}_read_{aid}", use_container_width=True):
112                if on_read:
113                    on_read(aid)

 1"""

10import plotly.graph_objects as go
11from typing import Dict, List, Any

13def plot_language_distribution(articles: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> go.Figure:
14    """Pie chart showing distribution of articles by language."""
15    lang_names = {"en": "English", "hi": "Hindi", "as": "Assamese"}
16    counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
17    for a in articles:
18        lang = lang_names.get(a.get("language"), a.get("language"))
19        counts[lang] = counts.get(lang, 0) + 1
20
21    fig = go.Figure(data=[
22        go.Pie(labels=list(counts.keys()), values=list(counts.values()), hole=0.38)
23    ])
24    fig.update_layout(
25        title="News Articles by Language",
26        template="plotly_white",
27        margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=40, b=20)
28    )
29    return fig
30
31def plot_category_distribution(articles: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> go.Figure:
32    """Bar chart showing distribution of articles by topic category."""
33    counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
34    for a in articles:
35        cat = a.get("category", "General").title()
36        counts[cat] = counts.get(cat, 0) + 1
37
38    fig = go.Figure(data=[
39        go.Bar(x=list(counts.keys()), y=list(counts.values()), marker_color="#3b82f6")
40    ])
41    fig.update_layout(
42        title="News Articles by Category",
43        xaxis_title="Category",
44        yaxis_title="Count",
45        template="plotly_white",
46        margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=40, b=20)
47    )
48    return fig
49
50def plot_baseline_comparison(baselines: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> go.Figure:
51    """Grouped bar chart comparing NDCG@5 and MRR@5 across paradigms."""
52    names = [b["config_name"] for b in baselines]
53    ndcg5 = [b["ndcg@5"] for b in baselines]
54    mrr5 = [b["mrr@5"] for b in baselines]
55
56    fig = go.Figure(data=[
57        go.Bar(name='NDCG@5', x=names, y=ndcg5, marker_color='#2563eb'),
58        go.Bar(name='MRR@5', x=names, y=mrr5, marker_color='#f97316')
59    ])
60    fig.update_layout(
61        title="Offline Evaluation: NDCG@5 and MRR@5 across Recommendation Paradigms",
62        xaxis_title="Recommender Paradigm",
63        yaxis_title="Score [0, 1]",
64        barmode='group',
65        template="plotly_white",
66        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1),
67        margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=50, b=20)
68    )
69    return fig
70
71def plot_diversity_gain() -> go.Figure:
72    """Bar chart comparing diversity metrics pre and post MMR."""
73    labels = ['Category Shannon Entropy', 'Pairwise Redundancy (Sim)', 'Unique Categories in Slate']
74    orig = [0.8113, 0.5050, 2.0]
75    mmr = [1.5000, 0.1683, 3.0]
76
77    fig = go.Figure(data=[
78        go.Bar(name='Before MMR (Relevance Only)', x=labels, y=orig, marker_color='#94a3b8'),
79        go.Bar(name='After MMR Diversification', x=labels, y=mmr, marker_color='#10b981')
80    ])
81    fig.update_layout(
82        title="Diversity & Redundancy Benchmark (MMR Trade-off)",
83        yaxis_title="Measured Index",
84        barmode='group',
85        template="plotly_white",
86        margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=40, b=20)
87    )
88    return fig

10def setup_logger(name: str = "NewsRecommender", level: int = logging.INFO) -> logging.Logger:
11    """Configure and return a structured console logger."""
12    logger = logging.getLogger(name)
13    if not logger.handlers:
14        logger.setLevel(level)
15        handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
16        handler.setLevel(level)
17        formatter = logging.Formatter(
18            fmt="[%(asctime)s] [%(levelname)s] [%(name)s]: %(message)s",
19            datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
20        )
21        handler.setFormatter(formatter)
22        logger.addHandler(handler)
23    return logger
24
25def cosine_similarity_matrix(a, b=None):
26    """
27    Compute cosine similarity matrix between row vectors of a and b.
28    Supports both NumPy ndarrays and pure Python nested lists.
29    """
30    try:
31        import numpy as np
32        if isinstance(a, np.ndarray):
33            if b is None:
34                b = a
35            a_norm = a / np.clip(np.linalg.norm(a, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-9, None)
36            b_norm = b / np.clip(np.linalg.norm(b, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-9, None)
37            return np.dot(a_norm, b_norm.T)
38    except ImportError:
39        pass
40
41    # Pure Python fallback
42    if b is None:
43        b = a
44
45    def norm(v):
46        val = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in v))
47        return val if val > 1e-9 else 1e-9
48
49    def dot(v1, v2):
50        return sum(x1 * x2 for x1, x2 in zip(v1, v2))
51
52    matrix = []
53    for row_a in a:
54        norm_a = norm(row_a)
55        res_row = []
56        for row_b in b:
57            norm_b = norm(row_b)
58            res_row.append(dot(row_a, row_b) / (norm_a * norm_b))
59        matrix.append(res_row)
60
61    return matrix
62
63def format_duration(seconds: float) -> str:
64    """Format duration in human-readable format."""
65    if seconds < 60:
66        return f"{seconds:.1f}s"
67    minutes = int(seconds // 60)
68    secs = int(seconds % 60)
69    return f"{minutes}m {secs}s"

 30class TestAdvancedIntelligencePhase6(unittest.TestCase):
 31    @classmethod
 32    def setUpClass(cls):

 34        cls.ref_time = datetime(2026, 11, 7, 12, 0, 0)

 36            temporal_lambda=0.23105,  # 3.0 days half life
 37            freshness_lambda=0.13863, # 5.0 days half life

 39        )

 48    def test_01_exponential_time_decay(self):
 49        """1. Verify exponential time decay formula: Weight = exp(-lambda * delta_days)."""
 50        lam = 0.23105
 51        # At delta = 0, decay must be exactly 1.0
 52        self.assertAlmostEqual(self.temporal_modeler.calculate_exponential_decay(0.0, lam), 1.0, places=5)
 53        # At delta = 3.0 days (half life), decay must be ~0.50
 54        decay_half = self.temporal_modeler.calculate_exponential_decay(3.0, lam)
 55        self.assertAlmostEqual(decay_half, 0.50, places=3)
 56        # At delta = 6.0 days, decay must be ~0.25
 57        decay_quarter = self.temporal_modeler.calculate_exponential_decay(6.0, lam)

Module Purpose: Phase 6 hyperparameter calibration and weight validation tests. 
 1"""
 2Test Mean-Centering Calibration and Contrastive Alignment on IndicBERT.
 3"""
 4
 5import sys
 6import json
 7import numpy as np
 8from pathlib import Path
 9
10# Add project root to sys.path
11PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
12sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))
13
14from src.embeddings.indicbert_encoder import IndicBERTEncoder
15
16def test_centering():
17    pairs_file = Path("data/evaluation/multilingual_eval_pairs.json")
18    with open(pairs_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
19        eval_pairs = json.load(f)
20
21    encoder = IndicBERTEncoder()
22
23    texts_as = [p["text1"] for p in eval_pairs if p["lang1"] == "as"]
24    texts_hi = [p["text2"] for p in eval_pairs if p["lang2"] == "hi"]
25    texts_en = [p["text2"] for p in eval_pairs if p["lang2"] == "en"]
26
27    embs_as = encoder.encode(texts_as, normalize_embeddings=False)
28    embs_hi = encoder.encode(texts_hi, normalize_embeddings=False)
29    embs_en = encoder.encode(texts_en, normalize_embeddings=False)
30
31    mu_as = np.mean(embs_as, axis=0)
32    mu_hi = np.mean(embs_hi, axis=0)
33    mu_en = np.mean(embs_en, axis=0)
34
35    print("Centering Results:")
36    calibrated_results = []
37    for p in eval_pairs:
38        e1 = encoder.encode(p["text1"], normalize_embeddings=False)
39        e2 = encoder.encode(p["text2"], normalize_embeddings=False)
40
41        mu1 = mu_as if p["lang1"] == "as" else (mu_hi if p["lang1"] == "hi" else mu_en)
42        mu2 = mu_as if p["lang2"] == "as" else (mu_hi if p["lang2"] == "hi" else mu_en)
43
44        c1 = (e1 - mu1) / (np.linalg.norm(e1 - mu1) + 1e-9)
45        c2 = (e2 - mu2) / (np.linalg.norm(e2 - mu2) + 1e-9)
46
47        sim_cal = float(np.dot(c1, c2))
48        raw_sim = float(np.dot(e1 / np.linalg.norm(e1), e2 / np.linalg.norm(e2)))
49        calibrated_results.append((p["pair_type"], p["is_equivalent"], raw_sim, sim_cal))
50        print(f"{p['id']:15s} [{p['pair_type']}] Equiv={p['is_equivalent']!s:5s} | Raw={raw_sim:.4f} -> Calibrated={sim_cal:+.4f}")
51
52    # Summary by pair type
53    print("\nCalibrated Separation Margin:")
54    for ptype in ["AS-AS", "AS-HI", "AS-EN", "HI-EN"]:
55        sub = [r for r in calibrated_results if r[0] == ptype]
56        eq_scores = [r[3] for r in sub if r[1]]
57        uneq_scores = [r[3] for r in sub if not r[1]]
58        if eq_scores and uneq_scores:
59            margin = np.mean(eq_scores) - np.mean(uneq_scores)
60            print(f"  {ptype}: Mean Equiv={np.mean(eq_scores):+.4f} | Mean Unrelated={np.mean(uneq_scores):+.4f} | Margin={margin:+.4f}")
61
62if __name__ == "__main__":
63    test_centering()

110            img = get_card_image(art["article_id"], art["category"])
111            self.assertEqual(img.size, (400, 240))
112        # Test unknown / missing article ID fallback
113        img_missing = get_card_image("art_missing_999", "science")
114        self.assertEqual(img_missing.size, (400, 240))

116    def test_08_multilingual_news_explorer_filters(self):
117        """8. Verify News Explorer filtering logic across English, Hindi, and Assamese."""

120        # Language filters

128        # Category filter

130        self.assertGreater(len(tech_arts), 0)
131
132        # Keyword search
133        search_query = "transformer"
134        matched = [a for a in articles if search_query in a["title"].lower() or search_query in a.get("abstract", "").lower()]
135        self.assertTrue(any(a["article_id"] == "art_en_001" for a in matched))
